title: RouteSafe: per-tenant batching & cache policy executor with staged validation
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Objective: Implement a safe, automated executor that applies per-customer and per-route batching/caching recommendations generated by Optimize. The executor (RouteSafe) must perform staged validation (dry-run -> shadow -> canary -> roll-forward) and provide deterministic diffs, fast rollback, and audit logs. This ticket covers the orchestration, policy fingerprints, verification gates, and runbook; kernel/runtime optimizations are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria:
1) RouteSafe can accept a policy bundle (batch.window, cache.allowlist/denylist, quantization-hint) and produce a deterministic plan diff prior to execution.
2) Dry-run mode produces simulated cost and latency deltas using historical traffic and synthetic sampling.
3) Shadow mode applies config to a mirror path with no user impact and reports measured deltas to a canary dashboard.
4) Canary rollouts support percent-based traffic (1%, 5%, 20%) and automated evaluation against pre-defined gates (latency p95, error-rate, token cost).
5) If any gate is violated, RouteSafe aborts and triggers automatic revert and on-call alert.
6) All actions are auditable (who/what/when), and config snapshots are stored for instant rollback.
7) End-to-end tests and a manual QA checklist are included in the PR.
rollout_plan:
Phase A - Dry-run (1 day): Run RouteSafe against last 7 days of traffic in simulator and publish cost/latency projection.
Phase B - Shadow (2 days): Apply configs to shadow paths for selected low-risk tenants (internal + 3 pilot customers). Collect real telemetry and compare.
Phase C - Canary (3 days): 1% -> 5% -> 20% traffic progression with automated gating at each step. Hold for 6 hours between steps and observe.
Phase D - Gradual roll-forward: 20% -> 50% -> 100% across tenant tiers, with manual approval at tier boundaries.
Safety knobs: max-allowed latency p95 increase = 2.0%, max-allowed 5xx delta = 0.1%, minimum expected cost saving = 3.0%. If savings < 3% within the canary window, the change is auto-marked for manual review (no auto-commit).
rollback_plan:
Automatic rollback: If any gate breaches during shadow or canary, RouteSafe executes immediate revert to last snapshot and notifies on-call with a short incident summary and links.
Manual rollback: Owners can trigger a one-click revert in Console which will reapply the previous policy snapshot.
Post-rollback: Run a quick postmortem task that includes telemetry diff and hypothesis; tag PR with 'safe-rollback' and create follow-up ticket for root cause.
TTL: Snapshots retained for 14 days in the fast-revert store, archived for 90 days in cold storage.
telemetry_and_gates:
Gates used by RouteSafe:
- latency_p95_change_percent (threshold 2.0%)
- 5xx_rate_change_absolute (threshold 0.1%)
- avg_tokens_per_request_change_percent (threshold 5%)
- cost_per_token_delta_percent (expect reduction > 3%)
Evaluation windows: 15m rolling (fast), 1h (stable). Alerts: Slack channel #route-safe-alerts and PagerDuty escalation if fast window triggers emergency revert.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: standalone orchestration service that talks to Router API, Console, and Optimize suggestion engine. Key pieces: Policy fingerprinting (to detect drift), Simulation engine (replay using sampler), Shadow adapter (mirror requests to canary path), Executor with idempotent apply and snapshotting.
Trade-offs: We intentionally keep conservative default gates to avoid false positives; advanced autotune will be a follow-up.
Database: store snapshots in config-store; include a compact binary diff to speed revert.
Testing: unit tests for plan diffing, e2e using internal loadbot, chaos experiments to validate revert under high concurrency.
Open questions: how to surface segmented allowlist conflicts when multiple policies overlap (per-route vs per-tenant). Proposed resolution: deterministic priority order and explicit conflict report in plan diff.
